read_population.measured_via: the sweep's own stderr and report.json; every one of the four paged reads (nodes + edges, per graph) reported complete=True and report.json's truncated_by is null

notes: REGENERATED 2026-08-27T06:51Z at 7a64b2a499, superseding the run at 8bc5f763a2. Reason: review found NODE_PAGE_CYPHER paging on `ORDER BY n.name`, which is not a total order and therefore violates _paged_ro_query's documented precondition. Re-measured live the same day: dark_factory holds 17260 Entity nodes against 17210 distinct names (50 duplicate-name groups), reify 24344 against 24193 (151 excess rows). At page_size 5000 that is 3 page boundaries in dark_factory and 4 in reify, and a tie straddling one drops a row while duplicating another — leaving rows_seen unchanged, so guard 4 never fires and the loss is invisible in truncated_by. Fixed to `RETURN n.uuid, n.name ORDER BY n.uuid`, matching graphiti_client.py::_ENTITY_NODES_PAGE_TEMPLATE exactly. ONLY the node read was affected; the edge read already ordered on r.uuid.

WHAT THE FIX CHANGED, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: nothing. Against the superseded 8bc5f763a2 artifact — findings 181 -> 181, the IDENTICAL set of 181 (edge_uuid, end) identities with zero added and zero removed; by_graph 76/105, by_end 108 subject / 73 object, by_proximity 97/8/0/76, and correct_node_present {true: 111, false: 70} all bit for bit unchanged, with ZERO correct_node_present flips among the 181 common findings. Only the live-corpus drift over the ~2h between runs moved: scanned 26667 -> 26674 (dark_factory 11411 -> 11418 rows, task-shaped nodes 1423 -> 1424; reify unchanged at 15256 / 2111), population 6959 -> 6961, unverifiable 304 -> 305, and rate 0.026009 -> 0.026002 purely via that denominator.

AND THE NULL RESULT WAS PREDICTED, WHICH IS WHY IT IS EVIDENCE RATHER THAN LUCK. The dropped row is always a TIE of a row that WAS returned — permuting equal-key rows can do nothing else — and under `ORDER BY n.name` two tied rows carry the same name and therefore the same task id. read_task_node_ids accumulates into a SET of ids, so the id set was immune to a read that was genuinely lossy. Stated as the prediction in the fix commit (89267aa047) BEFORE this run, and independently observed in test_a_tie_straddling_a_page_boundary_drops_a_node, where the id-set assertion passes while the per-record assertion fails. The review finding was correct about the defect and overstated about its consequence: the read could drop rows invisibly, but no published number was ever wrong because of it.

INHERITED FROM THE SUPERSEDED RUN (8bc5f763a2): that run itself regenerated an earlier sweep at 496b84cf4b/dff8c0ec58 to correct known_gaps' second direction-reversal specimen, which cited `01e3e75e` — a uuid that does not exist in reify in ANY state. The real edge is `01e3ff5d-ef73-4f52-9914-95533fca5cf9`, re-verified live over GRAPH.RO_QUERY and corroborated by docs/unverified-completion-claim-sweep-2026-08-11/report.json. The fix went into the script's KNOWN_GAPS literal, never into the artifact, which is what preserves the byte-for-byte property below.

report.json is byte-for-byte the script's stdout (cmp-verified against the captured stream, modulo the single trailing newline the --out-dir writer appends). Re-verified for this run with cmp against the captured stream: IDENTICAL, not merely equal modulo whitespace. It was neither pretty-printed nor hand-edited. All logging went to stderr.

DETERMINISM, MEASURED: the re-run 20 minutes later reproduced EVERY measured value bit for bit — scanned 26667, population 6959, unverifiable 304, findings 181, and the identical set of 181 edge uuids, plus identical by_graph/by_end/by_proximity/correct_node_present breakdowns. Only swept_at and the three corrected known_gaps lines differ. known_gaps is a static literal, not a measurement, so the correction moved no number. A THIRD snapshot at 06:51Z (this run, on the corrected node page) then reproduced the same 181 (edge_uuid, end) identities and the same by_graph / by_end / by_proximity / correct_node_present breakdowns, while scanned moved 26667 -> 26674, population 6959 -> 6961 and unverifiable 304 -> 305 with corpus growth. Note this is a stability observation over three nearby snapshots, NOT a guarantee: both graphs are written to continuously (see the LIVE CORPUS caveat in report.json), and the earlier planning-time measurement a few hours before did differ (192/7131).

PAGINATION IS LOAD-BEARING HERE AND THE RUN PROVES IT: reify returned 15256 live RELATES_TO rows through _paged_ro_query. The server's RESULTSET_SIZE is 10000, so an unpaginated MATCH — the shape audit_unverified_completion_claims.py uses, correctly, for its smaller population — would have returned exactly 10000 of them silently, and every denominator in this report would be wrong. This is why EdgeReader routes both reads through the shared paged primitive and why truncated_by is a first-class report key rather than a footnote.

AGREEMENT WITH THE PLANNING MEASUREMENT (2026-08-27, a few hours earlier, same branch): 181 findings over a 6961 population (2.60%) against the planning figures of 192/7131 (2.69%). Both graphs are written to continuously, so the denominator is a moving target and this is agreement, not drift. The two predicted families are both present: reify 'Task 6165' (6 findings here, 5 at planning time — the corpus grew) and dark_factory 'Task 430' (5). No extractor regression is indicated.

CAUSE EVIDENCE, RE-MEASURED ON THIS RUN: 105/181 (58%) of mis-bound endpoint ids fall in the near-miss proximity buckets (one_digit_diff 97, prefix 8, similar 0) against a chance baseline near zero over 1424 + 2111 task-shaped nodes (harvested by the CORRECTED uuid-ordered node page; 1423 + 2111 on the superseded name-ordered one, a delta of exactly the one node dark_factory gained between runs); and correct_node_present is true for 111/181 (61%), meaning the node the fact actually names ALREADY EXISTS in that graph in the majority of cases. Both figures reproduce the planning measurement (62.5% and 64%) within the movement of a live corpus. The second is the load-bearing one: this is predominantly ACTIVE mis-resolution, not a missing-node coverage gap.

THE CANONICAL SPECIMEN IS NOT REPRESENTATIVE, and the report carries both counts so that is visible: reify node 'Task 6164' does NOT exist, which puts the Task 6165 family in the 39% minority where the correct node is absent. A reader generalizing from that family alone would reach the wrong diagnosis.

BOTH ENDS ARE REPRESENTED: 108 subject-end and 73 object-end findings. The object-end population is what a subject-only detector — the one the task description proposes — would have missed entirely, and specimen 8a51e13b is in it.

SCOPE, STATED IN THE ARTIFACT ITSELF: report.json's known_gaps names the two sub-classes this Class-A detector provably does not cover (direction-reversal, specimens 1cf19488 / 01e3ff5d; and fact-contradicts-source-episode, specimen 993a9a7b) together with the measured refutation of the cheap leftmost-id direction heuristic. So 'this run found no reversals' cannot be read as 'the corpus holds no reversals'.

INVARIANT HELD: this sweep invalidated nothing, reassigned nothing and deleted nothing. Every edge the report names is left exactly as it is, for human adjudication. The script has no --apply/--invalidate/--delete/--repair/--reassign path, an absence pinned by TestReadOnlyByConstruction (whose forbidden-call set deliberately includes reassign_edge and merge_entities, the lossless remediation primitives for THIS defect class), and it reads the graph exclusively over GRAPH.RO_QUERY, where read-only is server-enforced.
